{{Short description|Japanese-American biochemist (1929–2020)}}
{{nihongo|'''Sen-itiroh Hakomori'''|箱守仙一郎|Hakomori Sen-itiroh|; 13 February 1929 – 10 November 2020}} was a Japanese-American biochemist.

Hakomori was born in [[Sendai]] on 13 February 1929, and graduated from [[Tohoku University]] Medical College in 1951. He elected for further study in biochemistry under Hajime Masamune. As a [[Fulbright Scholar]], Hakomori also worked with [[Roger W. Jeanloz]]. In 1959, Hakomori began teaching at the Tohoku College of Pharmaceutical Science.

Hakomori returned to the United States in 1964, again working under Jeanloz. In 1966, Hakomori joined the faculty of [[Brandeis University]]. He left Massachusetts two years later for a position at the [[University of Washington]].<ref>{{cite journal |last1=Fukuda |first1=Minoru |last2=Li |first2=Yu-Teh |last3=Schacter |first3=Harry |title=Editorial: Dr. Sen-itiroh Hakomori. |journal=Glycoconjugate Journal |date=April 1996 |volume=13 |issue=2 |pages=v–vii |doi=10.1007/BF00731484 |pmid=8737234|s2cid=32551888 }}</ref> Upon moving to Washington, Hakomori concurrently began work for the [[Fred Hutchinson Cancer Research Center]] and later the [[Pacific Northwest Research Institute]].<ref>{{cite journal |title=Biography of Professor Senitiroh Hakomori |journal=Glycoconjugate Journal |date=April 2003 |volume=20 |issue=3 |pages=147 |doi=10.1023/B:GLYC.0000024305.01534.39|s2cid=34463794 }}</ref> The Society for Glycobiology gave Hakomori its Karl Meyer Award in 1995.<ref>{{cite news |title=Sen-itiroh Hakomori: 1995 Karl Meyer Award Winner |url=http://glycobiology.org/Awards-Programs/Award-Winners/Sen-itiroh-Hakomori.aspx |accessdate=7 December 2018 |publisher=Society for Glycobiology |archive-date=7 December 2018 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20181207145624/http://glycobiology.org/Awards-Programs/Award-Winners/Sen-itiroh-Hakomori.aspx |url-status=dead }}</ref> He was elected member of the [[Finnish Society of Sciences and Letters]] in 1987<ref>{{Cite book|title=SPHINX Yearbook 2019-2020|publisher=Societas Scientiarum Fennica|year=2020|isbn=978-951-653-453-7|location=Helsinki}}</ref> and of the [[National Academy of Sciences]] in 2000.<ref>{{cite news |title=Sen-itiroh Hakomori |url=https://www.nasonline.org/directory-entry/sen-itiroh-hakomori-fmuoha/ |access-date=7 December 2018 |publisher=National Academy of Sciences}}</ref>  Hakomori shared the Society for Glycobiology's 2011 Rosalind Kornfeld Award with [[Yuan-Chuan Lee]].<ref>{{cite news |title=Sen-itiroh Hakomori wins 2011 Rosalind Kornfeld Award |url=http://glycobiology.org/Awards-Programs/Award-Winners/Sen-itiroh-Hakomori-(1).aspx |accessdate=7 December 2018 |publisher=Society for Glycobiology}}</ref>

He died at home in Mercer Island, Washington on November 10, 2020.<ref>{{cite news |title=OBITUARY Sen-itiroh Hakomori, 1929 – 2020, World Leader in Glycosphingolipid Research and Nobel Prize Nominee |url=https://www.napost.com/2020/obituary-sen-itiroh-hakomori-1929-2020-world-leader-in-glycosphingolipid-research-and-nobel-prize-nominee/ |accessdate=28 January 2020 |publisher=[[North American Post]]}}</ref>
